head.title: The system's documentation
head.lede: One book on what each part of the Compliance assistant does, why it is built that way and how the parts fit together. It is written for a reader who knows compliance work and does not want to read the code.

open.title: The whole book in one file
open.text: More than 500 pages with figures and tables, in Lithuanian and in English. The button opens the edition in the language you are reading now; for the other one, switch the language at the top of the page.
open.file: A PDF file in English, about 7 MB.

glance.name: The system at a glance
glance.text: What the system is for, the services it runs as, and the data it keeps.

ai.name: Artificial intelligence in the system
ai.text: The longest part. It follows the data from the law to the report: how a model is reached and what a call costs, how prompts are kept and changed, how the legal texts become a searchable corpus and a register of obligations, what is read out of a company's documents, how the compliance report is made and lives on, and how the chat assistant works. It ends with what keeps all of this trustworthy: the checks, the evaluation, the people who decide, and the cost.

running.name: Using and running the system
running.text: The console page by page, the API, security, deployment and operations, the tests, and how the system answers the course it was built for.

reference.name: Reference
reference.text: Every prompt, every chat tool, every act of the catalogue, the settings and a glossary.

acting.title: Who is acting
acting.text: A system that uses language models is only as trustworthy as the line it draws between what a model wrote, what the code verified and what a person decided. The book marks that line the same way on every page.

model.name: A model is asked
model.text: A yellow panel describes a call to a language model: what it is given, what it is told and what it must answer.

code.name: Code checks or computes
code.text: A blue panel describes what is done without a model: a quotation located in its document, a provision looked up in the corpus, a score computed. Nothing in it depends on what a model happened to say.

person.name: A person decides
person.text: A framed panel marks a decision the system never takes itself: approving the scope of a report, approving an obligation, signing a report off.
